newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Four Malaysia firms in downstream palm oil venture.
newsitem.headline: Four Malaysia firms in downstream palm oil venture.

text.p: Four Malaysian companies said in a joint statement on Wednesday that they have formed a consortium to invest in palm-based downstream activities.

The companies, Asiatic Development Bhd, Kuala Sidim Bhd, Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd's unit, IJM Plantations Sdn Bhd plans to initially invest 70 million ringgit to build a palm oil refinery and related facilities.
The plant in Sandakan town in eastern Sabah state will be financed by equity and bank borrowings.
Earthworks for the project is expected to start in the second half of this year and is expected to be commissioned within two years.
"When operational, the plant shall be assured of consistent supplies of raw materials from the parties' combined plantation landholdings of some 90,000 hectares in Sabah," the statement said.
The companies will participate equally in the joint firm Asiatic Vegetable Oils Refinery Sdn Bhd (AVOR), currently a wholly-owned unit of Asiatic.
AVOR will be used to establish a palm oil refinery, palm kernel crusher and oleochemical plants, oil packaging and other related manufacturing facilities, the statement said.
